issues.description: Attribute 'lectureName' has conflicting types between the exercise specification and the provided solution. The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) specifies lectureName: String (UML class Lecture, attribute lectureName: String). In the solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the field is declared as private LectureName lectureName; and the constructor also takes a LectureName parameter. This mismatch (expected String vs. solution using a LectureName object) makes the required student-facing type unclear and also causes further inconsistencies inside the solution: the solution's getters/setters and constructor use String in their signatures while the field is LectureName, which leads to compilation errors and confuses students implementing the class according to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent across artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to use String for lectureName (change the field to 'private String lectureName;', change the constructor parameter to String, and ensure getters/setters return/accept String), which matches the UML and the exercise text; or (B) update the problem statement/UML to document that lectureName is a LectureName value object and adjust the UML, task text and example outputs accordingly. Also fix the solution's getter/setter signatures to match the chosen field type so the code compiles (e.g., if keeping LectureName, change getLectureName() to return LectureName and setLectureName(LectureName)).
